patch.value: pm-vcs becomes a version control system in its own right, not a helper around git

The 2026.7.30 package is a git companion: it audits merge-driver configuration, predicts what pm-cli's merge driver would resolve, and joins a commit range to the items it touched. Useful, but it owns no history - every fact it reports is read back out of git. This epic makes pm-vcs an actual VCS with its own object store, refs, working tree, diff, and merge, written from scratch with no shell-out to git and no git-compatible format. The reason to build one rather than use git: git merges lines. Project data is structured records, which is why pm-cli needs merge drivers bolted onto git at all. A VCS that stores records natively can merge them per field, so many agents on many branches converge without the line-merge hazard existing anywhere in the pipeline. The shipped git-interop surface is kept and moves under a git subcommand group.

pm-vcs can init a repository, stage and commit content, branch, switch, diff any two revisions, and three-way merge with a correctly computed merge base, entirely through its own code; structured records merge per field rather than per line; every mutating operation is recorded in an operation log that undo can rewind; two repositories can exchange history through an export/import bundle; no code path shells out to git for any of it; 100 percent line, branch and function coverage

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Engine complete and functionally verified against real repositories: 26 end-to-end checks over init, stage, commit, branch, switch, merge (clean, fast-forward, up-to-date, conflicted), undo, bundle round-trip, compare-and-swap refusal and dirty-switch refusal; plus 15 checks over the per-field record path. Myers diff property-checked over 4000 random line-pair inputs in both directions. Two bugs caught during construction worth recording: computeStatus originally called store.write to hash a working file, so asking for status left every unstaged revision in the object store; and readWorkingFile used statSync, which follows symlinks, making its own symlink branch unreachable. A third was a false optimisation - the index carried a size field used to short-circuit change detection, which reported every reformat of a canonicalised record path as a modification. readWorkingFile has already read the whole file by that point, so hashing it costs less than the read did; the field was removed rather than repaired.
